patients.label: 58-year-old woman with esophageal perforation and persistent fistula after anterior cervical C5-C6 surgery, repaired with an SCM muscle flap

identity_evidence.quote: A 58-year-old women presented with symptomatic cervical neck and left arm pain.

attribution_limitations: The discussion says the diagnosis was made two days after surgery, whereas the case narrative places symptom onset on the second postoperative day and worsening over the following 48 hours before the Gastrograffin swallow. The exact day of the swallow study is not stated.
The decision to remove the cervical plate is stated ("we decide to remove"), but the source does not explicitly say the plate was removed.

The "11th postoperative day" at discharge is not explicitly anchored to an operation; the paragraph context suggests the repair operation, while the earlier "second postoperative day" refers to the first (cervical spine) operation.
The article does not state an anchor for "After one month" at the flexible endoscopic control (surgery, discharge, or the end of the stay).
The caption says the fistula was closed with 3-0 Vicryl; the case text describes absorbable stitches without naming the material, so the link between the two is the caption only.

The contrast swallow control sentence reads "fell to demonstrate", most plausibly a print error for "failed to demonstrate"; the result is recorded as no sign of esophageal rent because oral intake and discharge followed, but the literal wording is defective.

claims.text: A 58-year-old woman presented with cervical neck and left arm pain. MRI showed a prominent left sided C5-C6 disc herniation compressing the spinal cord and nerve root. She underwent a C5-C6 discectomy through an antero-lateral left cervical approach with interbody iliac bone graft and anterior cervical plate fixation.

evidence.quote: A 58-year-old women presented
symptomatic cervical neck and left arm pain
MRI of the cervical spine demonstrating prominent left sided C5-C6 disc herniation causing spinal cord and nerve root compression.
She underwent by an antero-lateral left side cervical approach a C5-C6 dissectomy with interbody iliac bone graft and anterior cervical plate fixation.
C5-C6 dissectomy with interbody iliac bone graft
anterior cervical plate fixation

claims.text: On the morning of the second postoperative day she developed dysphonia, dysphagia and cervical swelling. Over the next 48 hours she became pyretic and moderately dyspnoic, dysphagia turned into odynophagia and subcutaneous emphysema of the neck appeared. Gastrograffin swallow x-ray showed signs of a pharyngo-esophageal rent with contrast leakage into the upper mediastinum.

evidence.quote: On the morning of the second postoperative day, she started to complain of dysphonia and dysphagia and presented a cervical swelling at the surgical incision site.

Over the next 48 hours period, her clinical conditions worsened: she was found pyretic and moderately dyspnoic, the dysphagia turned into odynophagia, whereas the localized swelling diffused in the form of a mantle like subcutaneous emphysema of the neck.
Gastrograffin swallow x-ray demonstrated signs of a pharyngo-esophageal rent as leakage of the contrast mean into the upper mediastinum (Figure 1).
By a left lateral cervical approach, the fistula tract ahead of the neurovascular pedicle was followed deeply to the left lateral pharyngo-esophageal rent (Figure 2).

claims.text: Conservative treatment with wide-spectrum antibiotics, nasogastric enteral feeding and a cervical subcutaneous drain gave only partial amelioration, and the suction tube still drained corpuscolated material. Esophagoscopy showed the plate outside a thinner esophageal wall. The fistula persisted after 45 days, so she was taken to the operating room, where the rent was found corresponding to the previously placed cervical column-blocking device.

evidence.quote: A consecutive attempted conservative approach, by administering wide-spectrum antibiotics, enteral feeding by nasogastric tube and a cervical subcutaneous drain led to only partial clinical amelioration, reduced the cervical swelling, but still the suction tube at the cervical surgical site draining corpuscolated material.
led to only partial clinical amelioration, reduced the cervical swelling
but still the suction tube at the cervical surgical site draining corpuscolated material

As the fistula still persisted even after 45 days of conservative treatment and disapearance of inflamation, the patient was taken to the operating room.
The latter was found corresponding to the previously placed cervical column-blocking device.

claims.text: The rent was primarily sutured in two layers and a superiorly based SCM muscle flap was interposed between the esophagus and the cervical column. Contrast swallow control showed no sign of rent, she started liquids by mouth and was discharged on the 11th postoperative day. After one month endoscopy confirmed absence of perforation and she was taking a normal oral diet.

evidence.quote: The rent was primarily sutured with a reinforced 2-layer (mucosal and muscular) row of separated absorbable stitches.
A superiorly based SCM muscular flap was then elevated, medially rotated and interposed between the esophagus and the cervical column to protect the viscus repair (Figure 3).
